files.why: Add a pure, framework-free matchesInvoiceQuery(invoice, query) predicate — which fields count as searchable is a domain decision, so it belongs in core (testable, no Vue).
Hold the search query ref, debounce it via @shared/lib/useDebounce, and expose a filteredInvoices computed built from the core predicate.
Render the @shared/ui/input search box bound to the query and iterate the debounced filtered list instead of the raw one.
Add a pure matchesAppointmentQuery(appointment, query) predicate mirroring billing, keeping searchable-field logic framework-free and testable.
Hold the search query ref, debounce it, and expose a filtered appointments computed using the core predicate.
Render the shared Input search box bound to the query and iterate the debounced filtered appointment list.
Cover the new matchesInvoiceQuery predicate (match/no-match, case-insensitivity, empty query) — final-phase test for the added core logic.
Cover the new matchesAppointmentQuery predicate the same way.

uncertain: Whether the match predicate belongs in core/rules.ts or inline in the composable. I chose core because 'which fields are searchable' is a domain decision and the README's example 1 routes new logic to core/rules.ts (plus core has existing test files). Counter-argument: a plain substring text filter is arguably generic presentational UI, in which case it could live purely in the composable and skip the two core-rules and two test-file edits.

Whether 'both list views' means InvoiceListView + DayView. DayView is scheduling's only list-like view but it's titled 'Day schedule' and shows one fixed day, not an obvious 'list'; the app-level ClientOverviewView renders two lists (unpaid invoices / upcoming appointments) but is a dashboard, not a filterable list. I assumed the two slice list views and excluded ClientOverviewView.

Whether filtering must stay client-side. Both views already load their full dataset client-side, so a debounced client-side filter never touches the server at all and satisfies 'without hammering the server' trivially; debounce then only guards recompute/future server use. If the team actually wants server-side search, data/queries.ts, data/mocks.ts, and (for billing) data/store.ts would also need changes and the debounce becomes load-bearing.
questions: What should each search actually match on? Neither model carries human-readable text: Invoice has only number + clientId (no client name), and Appointment has only clientId + resourceId + times (no title/name). Do you want to match invoice number and appointment resource/client ids, or should the API/read-models first expose names to search against?

Is client-side filtering over the already-loaded lists acceptable, or do you require server-side search (which would add query params to data/queries.ts + MSW mocks + billing's cache store and make the debounce necessary rather than just prudent)?
Does 'both list views' mean the billing InvoiceListView and scheduling DayView specifically, or should the app-level ClientOverviewView dashboard lists get search boxes too?
Preferred debounce delay — is the shared useDebounce default of 300ms fine?
